notes: 1868 Greek grammar (test split) packed with letter-level examples, stem hyphenation and paradigms. Plain prose lines read correctly (5, 6, 9, 10, 16, 19, 20), but the examples are often wrong and the errors are mostly unflagged: 'ἀμπέλω' for ἀμπέχω (1), 'μὲ πρὸ τοῦ ἐἢ' for 'μ πρὸ τοῦ λ ἢ' (3), 'μμ' for μ (4), 'ἐημάτων' for ῥημάτων (27), 'Ἀργός' for Ἀρνός (23), 'εἶνεν ἢ ρ' for 'εἶνε ν ἢ ρ' (31), and breathing errors in the 'Οἷς, οἰός' paradigm (22). Several crops also don't match their labels (8 and 30 truncated, 26/38 two lines merged, 40 a fragment of another line). About a quarter of the random sample is wrong, which is too much for a test book, and no simple rule isolates the errors.
